correctness.rationale: The stationary characteristic function satisfies (Lambda+A k²+B l²)Phi=c+a/(1+l²)+b/(1+k²), where A=a+c, B=b+c, Lambda=a+b+c. It gives a strictly positive three-component mixture of an exponential-aged anisotropic Gaussian H with optional independent Laplace addition to one coordinate. Gaussian-age integration yields J0=sqrt(Lambda(u²/A+v²/B)); contraction of Laplace costs yields Jx and Jy via convex scalar minimization. Their active regions produce exactly I=y+x sqrt(a/A) for x/y<=sqrt(Aa)/B, central sqrt(Lambda(x²/A+y²/B)) between rays, and I=x+y sqrt(b/B) for x/y>=A/sqrt(Bb). Rate strictly increases in both positive coordinates, giving the orthant exceedance limit; derivatives match at the two boundaries but transverse second derivatives jump. At fixed A,B, the ellipse-box support function shrinks strictly as c increases, and every positive-direction maximizer meets the ellipse so I strictly decreases. Generator moments yield Cov(U²,V²)=4c/Lambda. Independent computations compared 550 arbitrary rate samples to direct scalar minimization and 450 strict order samples; these are finite corroborations of the analytical LDP and monotonicity.

limitations: Only strictly positive independent Poisson clocks and independent Brownian free motions with reset to zero; unequal a,b is the assessed contribution.
